Group Discussion after Astarion is revealed to be a vampire and has been chased off or killed.3 role (Should've seen it/Kinda Fun/Dangerous)   1: Wyll/Laezel/Karlach   2: Karlach/Shadowheart/Gale   3: Laezel/Gale   4: Player Avatar2 role (Kinda Fun/Dangerous)   1: Karlach/Wyll/Shadowheart/Gale   2: Gale/Laezel   3: Player Avatar1 role (Laezel)   1: Laezel   2: Player Avatar1 Role (Kinda Fun)   1: Karlach/Gale/Shadowheart/Wyll   2: Player Avatar0 Role (LoneWolf narration)

Cluster Contexts:
- GLO_Astarion_GD_VampireRevelation.json: The party is gathered at camp after Astarion’s vampiric nature was exposed and he was driven off (or possibly killed), and everyone is hashing over what happened. Off‑screen, Astarion has been flirting with danger for a while — showing off after fights, admitting to feeding on animals and once trying or attempting to bite a companion at night — and he’s long had a traumatic past under a cruel master that explains his hunger and boldness. The Player’s lines show mixed feelings: fondness for Astarion’s cleverness and charm, but anger that he endangered the whole camp by trying to “open” someone’s neck. Companions in the scene will therefore be split between treating the revelation as a lesson in caution, amusement at Astarion’s audacity, or serious alarm at the risk he posed.
- ORI_AstarionIsAVamp_PAD_GaleWasBitten.json: Off-screen, Astarion has just tried to bite Gale (or had bitten him earlier at camp in some branches) and recoiled because Gale’s blood tasted foul — the bite makes Astarion appear sick or poisoned. Depending on the branch, this moment either exposes Astarion’s vampiric nature to the rest of the party or happens after they already knew he was a vampire. Gale’s lines are wry and reproachful (mocking the feeding, telling Astarion to ask first, or scolding him for hiding his nature), consistent with his bookish, sardonic tone. The exchange ties back to Astarion’s established vampire‑spawn background (his history with Cazador) and can be further shaped by prior events such as a camp feeding, who’s in the party, or earlier revelations.
- Astarion_InParty2_Nested_BlackMassFollowUp.json: Section of the Astarion's In Party dialog where we discuss the aftermath of the Black Mass Ritual (Astarion became vampire lord or stayed vampire spawn, possible romance/friendship discussions)
- ORI_AstarionIsAVamp_PAD_KarlachWasBitten.json: Off‑screen, during gameplay Astarion tried to feed on Karlach and took a small bite, but her blood/heat reacted painfully and burned him. That moment can serve as an exposure: if the party didn’t already know he’s a vampire, companions (and Karlach) are shocked and the bite reveals his nature; if they already knew, Karlach instead teases that she’s “too hot” for him. These lines are short, in‑party, reactive quips triggered immediately after the bite and draw on Astarion’s vampiric history and existing party dynamics; other companions (e.g., Lae’zel or Gale) may have their own topical responses off‑screen.
- CAMP_AstarionHungerC_CRD_Astarion_MorningAfter.json: You wake the morning after the night Astarion tried to bite you — depending on your previous choices he either did so with your consent or you told him to piss off. Astarion is a companion and a vampire spawn, so he'll be cautious this morning to gauge whether you're still forgiving or ready to punish him. Other companions may chime in with judgement or concern about having a vampire in the party, and some follow-up lines only appear once you or they learn more about Astarion. Off-screen background that matters: Astarion was enslaved to a master (Cazador) and bears carved scars from that past, and he’s been preoccupied with dark books and secrets that make him edgy.

context: The party is gathered at camp immediately after Astarion’s vampiric nature was exposed and he was driven off or killed. Off‑screen, he’s long flirted with danger — showing off after fights, feeding on animals, and even trying to bite companions — and he bears scars and trauma from having been enslaved to a cruel master (Cazador). The Player feels conflicted: admiring Astarion’s charm and cleverness but angry that he endangered the whole camp by trying to “open” someone’s neck. Companions are split between amusement at his audacity, stern alarm about the risk, and a resolve to be more cautious going forward; in some branches Gale or Karlach were bitten and reacted badly (Gale’s blood tasting foul, Karlach’s heat burning him), which either exposed Astarion or heightened the shock.
